questions.question: Which of the following is the PRIMARY purpose of an internal audit charter?

options.A: To define the audit function's purpose, responsibility, authority and accountability
options.B: To describe the detailed procedures used in each audit engagement
options.C: To list the findings of previous audits
options.D: To set the IT department's annual budget

questions.explanation: The charter is a high-level document, approved by the board or audit committee, that establishes the audit function's mandate, authority and accountability. Detailed procedures belong in audit programs, not in the charter.

questions.question: What is the MAIN benefit of using a risk-based approach when building the annual audit plan?

options.A: Audit resources are focused on the areas that present the highest risk to the organization
options.B: The total cost of auditing is always reduced
options.C: Every control in the organization is tested each year
options.D: The need for audit sampling is eliminated

questions.explanation: Audit resources are limited; a risk-based plan allocates them where the potential impact on the organization is greatest. It does not guarantee lower cost, full coverage or the absence of sampling.

questions.question: Compared with judgmental (non-statistical) sampling, statistical sampling allows the IS auditor to:

options.A: Objectively quantify sampling risk and the confidence level of the conclusion
options.B: Avoid documenting the sample selection method
options.C: Guarantee that the population contains no errors
options.D: Select only the items the auditor considers most risky

questions.explanation: Statistical sampling uses probability theory, so the auditor can express the sampling risk and confidence level mathematically. Choosing the riskiest items on purpose is judgmental sampling, and no sampling method can guarantee an error-free population.

questions.question: The recovery point objective (RPO) PRIMARILY defines:

options.A: The maximum acceptable amount of data loss, expressed as a period of time
options.B: The maximum acceptable downtime before operations must resume
options.C: The time needed to activate the alternate processing site
options.D: The geographic distance required between primary and backup sites

questions.explanation: The RPO is the point in time to which data must be recovered, i.e. how much data loss is tolerable; it drives backup and replication frequency. The maximum acceptable downtime is the recovery time objective (RTO).

questions.question: Which of the following combinations provide genuine multi-factor authentication? (choose all that apply)

options.A: A password plus a one-time code generated by a hardware token
options.B: A fingerprint scan plus a PIN
options.C: A password plus the answer to a security question
options.D: Two different passwords entered one after the other

questions.explanation: Multi-factor authentication combines factors of different types: something you know, something you have, something you are. Options C and D only combine two items of the same type (something you know), so they remain single-factor.

questions.question: Which of the following situations represents the GREATEST segregation of duties concern?

options.A: A developer can modify source code and also move it into the production environment
options.B: A help desk analyst resets user passwords after verifying the caller's identity
options.C: A database administrator maintains the data dictionary
options.D: A security administrator reviews firewall logs

questions.explanation: Allowing the same person to change code and promote it to production bypasses change management: unauthorized or malicious changes could reach production undetected. The other situations are normal duties for those roles.
